html:
The Afanasievo culture was an early herding culture of south Siberia, in the Altai Mountains and the Minusinsk Basin on the upper Yenisei, from about 3300 to 2500 BCE. It is named after a hill in Khakassia where it was first dug.

Its people kept cattle, sheep and goats, used some copper, and buried their dead under low round mounds. Their graves, skulls and genes are very close to those of the Yamnaya culture of the steppes north of the Black Sea, some 2,000 kilometres to the west. So they were probably part of a fast early spread of herders east across the Eurasian steppe.

Many scholars link the Afanasievo people with the speakers of the Tocharian languages, an Indo-European branch later found in the Tarim Basin of Xinjiang. In the Minusinsk Basin they were followed by the Okunev culture, and later the region was part of the Andronovo world.
